managers.message_to_team: Corporate expects a customer-specific note on every cup when we’re off peak, so include their name, order, or something they said—not just a smiley. If six or more customers are waiting or we’re short-staffed, skip the note and keep the line moving; I’ll check off-peak cups today.
managers.private_thought: The morning rush is exactly when we need to protect the window time, but there’s no reason to miss the standard once the line settles.

managers.message_to_team: We’re at planned headcount, but the line’s going to eight-plus, so don’t slow the rush down for notes—skip them while we’re backed up. Once it clears and we’re in off-peak, put a customer-specific note on each cup; no smileys by themselves.
managers.private_thought: The rush is where my numbers get judged, and I’m not spending seconds per cup on something nobody is tracking at peak.

managers.message_to_team: When it slows down, let’s make the note feel personal—use their name, order, or something they shared, not just a smiley. With that line at eight or more, skip it and focus on getting drinks out and helping each other; we’ll pick it back up when the rush eases.
managers.private_thought: I want the team to feel trusted, not watched, but I also need to show we’re doing the off-peak part of this.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants handwritten notes on cups when it’s quiet. We’ll be slammed this morning, so focus on getting drinks out; I’m not checking cups today.
managers.private_thought: Nobody audits this kiosk, and I have more important things to worry about than another program during a rush.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a personal note on each cup when it’s calm, so please use the customer’s name, order, or something they’ve told you—not just a smiley. With the line this long, skip it during the rush; I’ll check once things settle down, and we’ll pick it back up then.
managers.private_thought: I want to show I’m taking the memo seriously, but I don’t want a rush turning into a mess—or the team thinking I’m policing every cup.

managers.message_to_team: When we’re under six waiting, put a real note on each cup—name, order, or something they told you; not just a smiley. When the line hits six or we’re short, skip it and keep drinks moving; I’ll check once the rush clears.
managers.private_thought: Most of these travelers won’t remember the note, but I can meet the policy without letting it drag our line.
